newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to take delivery of French warplanes-radio.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to take delivery of French warplanes-radio.

text.p: Taiwan will take delivery of an initial batch of Mirage 2000-5 fighter jets from France in the next two days to bolster its defences against arch rival China, state radio reported on Tuesday.
An undisclosed number of Mirages were expected to arrive at northern Keelung port on Wednesday or Thursday, the report said, quoting unnamed Defence Ministry sources.
"The planes are to be shipped here all right, but I cannot confirm the date of their arrival," a ministry official told Reuters by telephone.

Local press had reported that France decided to move forward the delivery of an initial batch of the warplanes by one month to April to minimise pressure from China when President Jacques Chirac visits Beijing in May.

Taiwan ordered 60 of the advanced French warplanes in a 1992 deal that caused a serios rift between France and China, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949.
Paris patched things up with Beijing by promising two years later to end arms sales to Taiwan, but has pledged to honour the Mirage contract.
Paris recognises Beijing and has no diplomatic ties with Taiwan's exiled Republic of China government.
